CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  SPECIAL MEETING
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY COMMISSION

  City Hall, 111 South First Street
  November 16, 2023
  6:00 p.m.

  I.  ROLL CALL
  Lisa Massaro, Kim Luu, Katie Chan, Yvette Corona

  II.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY MEETING MINUTES
  Commission Members will vote to approve 9-14-23 meeting minutes.
  Recommended Action: Approve the meeting minutes.

  III.  UPDATE ITEMS
  a) Bike and Pedestrian Plan
  b) Turf Replacement Rebate
  c) Organic Waste Recycling Program.
  d) Safe Clean Water Program
  Recommended Action: Information only. No action required

  IV.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN PRESENTATION
  The Environmental Sustainability Plan Consultant, ESA, will provide a project overview, existing
  conditions update and community engagement strategy for the City’s Sustainability Plan.
  Recommended Action: Information and discussion. No action required.

  V.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments are welcome, but
  must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please
  limit all oral communication to five (5) minutes. Speakers must fill out a blue speaker’s card, prior
  to the meeting and submit it to the Commission Secretary. Comments must pertain to the business
  of the Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit all oral communications to five (5)
  minutes.

  VI.  ORGANICS WASTE RECYCLING PRESENTATION
  On November 2, 2023, the City launched the new Alhambra Recycles Campaign, an initiative
  aimed at improving community and business participation in the City’s organics recycling program.
  Joris Eigirdas, the City’s Recycling Assistant, will present the various components of the robust
  campaign.
  Recommended Action: Information and discussion. No action required

  VII.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments are welcome, but
  must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please
  limit all oral communication to five (5) minutes. Speakers must fill out a blue speaker’s card, prior
  to the meeting and submit it to the Commission Secretary. Comments must pertain to the business
  of the Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit all oral communications to five (5)
  minutes.

 VIII.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the Commission Members of any item not specified on the agenda and agenda
  items for next meeting. Items must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental
  Sustainability Commission.
  Recommended Action: Discussion only. No action required.

IX.  ADJOURNMENT
  Adjournment to the next regular meeting on Thursday, January 11, 2024 at 6:00 p.m.

If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it to
the secretary. When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please
make your statement as brief as possible. The maximum time for addressing the Committee is five minutes.

If you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be
heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Committee on a subject
which does not appear on the agenda, but is of an environmental concern, your comments will be heard
under Public Comments. Please be advised that under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, the
Commission cannot take action on any item which does not appear on the agenda.

Copies of staff reports or other written documentation, if any, relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the Alhambra City Hall, Public Works Department, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra
California 91801 and are available for public inspection upon request during regular business hours of
7:00am to 5:30pm, Monday through Thursday.

Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting
described herein, he or she may contact David Dolphin, Deputy Director of Utilities, either in person at the
Utilities Department at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, or by calling via telephone at (626) 570-
5067 during regular business hours.

  MINUTES
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting of September 14, 2023

  The regular meeting of the Environmental Sustainability Commission was called to
  order at 6:05 p.m. on September 14, 2023.

•  Roll Call
  Commission Members Present: Chan, Massaro, Corona

  Commission Members Absent: Luu

  Staff Present:  David Dolphin – Commission Secretary

  Members of the Public

  Sandy Lee

•  VOTE TO APPROVE MEETING MINUTES FROM 5/11/23 AND 7/13/23
  Commissioner Chan motioned to approve the meeting minutes from 5/11/23 and
  7/13/23. Commissioner Massaro seconded the motion. All Commissioners present
  voted in favor to approve the minutes. Motion to approve passed.

  Commission Chan prepared to chair the meeting and review the agenda items.

•  UPDATE ITEMS
  Provided in the Agenda packets and verbally provided by City staff:

  1. Sustainability and Bike & Pedestrian Plans
  • Consultants and City staff continue to gather data in relation to examining
  environmental sustainability opportunities in Alhambra. As part of the
  process, the development of the City’s plan will also include stakeholder
  outreach and community engagement to better understand the
  community’s needs and concerns. The schedule for such outreach is
  anticipated for the Fall of 2023.
  Meanwhile, staff attended the California Adaptation Forum, featuring
  much discussion about sustainability and climate adaptation. These are
  important opportunities to learn from environmental experts and practices
  from other jurisdictions. Heat mitigation was at the center of many
  conversations.

  Page 1 of 7
   ITEM #2
  •  The development of the Bike and Pedestrian Plan draft continues, with
  release of the plan for public review tentatively in the Fall of 2023. Alta
  Planning and staff continue to evaluate bike and ped improvement
  concepts, network, and locations. In July 2023, staff worked with the
  consultant to identify some bike and pedestrian improvement opportunities
  along the south end of the City for the purposes of qualifying for the
  Metro Express Lanes Round 3 Net Toll Revenue Reinvestment Grant
  Program. Authorization to apply was submitted to the City Council at the
  July 24, 2023 meeting. Details of the City’s improvement are identified in
  the staff report. In summary, the grant request includes bike and ped
  improvements at Poplar Boulevard and Palm Avenue; Marguerita Avenue;
  Corto Street and Almansor Street; Chapel Avenue; South Alhambra
  Greenway; and Alhambra Road. The majority of the work is for “quick
  build” to enable quick and affordable installation and to further engage the
  community before permanent changes are installed. If awarded, the grants
  funds will be announced in October 2023.

2. Turf Replacement Rebate
  The San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District (SGVMWD) has submitted the
  application for the DWR Drought Relief Grant to provide assistance to its
  member agencies to fund a turf replacement rebate program. There has been no
  movement from the state since our last meeting.
3. Organic Waste Recycling Program
  • The City hosted two Organics Recycling Workshops for Alhambra
  residents on 8.23.2023 at Reese Hall. Participants learned the importance
  of organics recycling, how to separate their waste properly, tips to
  maintain cleanliness of their containers, and additional programs offered
  to residents by Republic Services. Residents that were unable to attend are
  encouraged to access resources on bit.ly/alhambrarecycles. The City plans
  to have another workshop in the Winter.
  • LA County hosted a Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) Collection
  Event on 8.26.2023 at their LA Public Works Headquarters building in
  Alhambra. Residents that missed this event are encouraged to visit
  https://www.cityofalhambra.org/667/Household-Hazardous-Waste and
  utilize the City of Los Angeles’ HHW permanent collection sites, which
  are available for free to all LA County residents year-round.
  • New resources to increase participation in the City’s organics recycling
  program through behavior change, including a “Compost Charlie
  Recycling Game,” are available to residents at bit.ly/alhambrarecycles.
  Additional resources and content to come soon.
  • The City is hosting a Compost Giveaway Event on 9.30.2023 from 9AM
  to 12PM at Granada Park. Please note that unlike previous years, compost
  giveaway service is a separate event from our Alhambra Recycles Event.
  Be sure to bring your own container. More information at
  bit.ly/alhambrarecycles. Flyer included in Agenda Packet

  Page 2 of 7
   ITEM #2
  •  The City is hosting their bi-annual Alhambra Recycles Event on 10.7.2023
  from 8AM to 12PM at Granada Park. Residents are able to recycle
  electronic waste, plastic bottles, and aluminum cans, and shred documents
  on-site. Compost will be given away at a separate event on 9.30.2023.
  First 175 participants will receive a free Fosselman’s Ice Cream scoop
  voucher. More information at bit.ly/alhambrarecycles.
  Flyer included in Agenda Packet
  •  The City and Republic Services are hosting an Organics Recycling
  Workshop for Alhambra businesses on 11.16.2023. Businesses will learn
  about new requirements for organics recycling and food recovery and
  exchange tips on best practices. More information to come.

4. Safe Clean Water Program (SCWP)

  The City has submitted an application for funding the following stormwater
  capture projects:
  • Green Street Demonstration Project on Main St – Application was
  submitted to the Safe Clean Water Program FY 2024-25 call for projects
  by the deadline, July 31, 2023. We are seeking funding for construction
  and operations & maintenance costs. The City received a $3M Urban
  Greening Grant.
  • A Request for Proposals for design was released on 7/27/23. A total of 3
  proposals were received and are currently under review.

5. Refill Stores

  The City of Alhambra Grant Specialist is not aware of any grant opportunities that
  are available for Refill Stores. One of the reasons could be these markets are
  privately owned and for profit.

  The City of Alhambra’s Economic Development Specialist did not receive
  inquiries from anyone expressing interest in opening a refill store. The City
  would welcome these establishments and will keep an eye open for opportunities.
  Contact Tiffany Chew, Economic Development Specialist, 626-570-5038 if you
  know of anyone interested in opening a refill store in Alhambra.

  Commissioner Corona Asked how did they reach out for inquires? Staff
  responded Tiffany did not reach out for inquiries regarding refill stores but she is
  open to the idea. The City is definitely open to having a refill store open for
  residents. Also, if anyone is aware of a refill store that would like to open a
  business in Alhambra, please have them contact Tiffany.

  Commissioner Chan – For clarification purposes for the Bike and Pedestrian Plan
  the streets listed are the temporary locations, are those streets the only street?
  Staff advised the Plan applies to the entire City and those streets indicated just
  applied to the Transportation Grant for a quick build. The Bike and Pedestrian
  Plan is looking for connectivity with the least amount of danger. An online

  Page 3 of 7
   ITEM #2
  survey was conducted and the Plan will go out for Public Comment before it is
  finalized.

  The Commission would like to see how the streets listed work out before they
  provided comments. The Staff Report on the 7/24/23 Council meeting will have
  information on the Plan.

  Commissioner Chan wanted clarification for HHW sites. Staff advised HHW stands
  for Household Hazardous Waste and the events are open to all LA County residents
  which are year-round at different locations.

  Commissioner Corona - Wanted to know if the agenda was transferred over from the
  last meeting and it was confirmed by staff.

•  ALHAMBRA TREE ORDINANCE

  Commissioners began to discuss their ideas on how to draft a stronger tree
  preservation ordinance in order to save native trees and push to replace grass in front
  yards with California Native Plants.

  Commissioner Chan wanted to know if the tree preservation ordinance applied to City
  trees. Staff confirmed the ordinance applied to City trees as well. Commission Chan
  wanted to push for city staff member to adopt a stronger ordinance. Staff advised
  Community Development is tasked with enforcing the ordinance and if changes are
  recommended, they should present them to the City Council for approval. During
  this meeting, Commissioners will review the ordinance and identify the changes
  necessary to be made to make it stronger.

  Commissioner Chan – Referring to the last sentence of 20.88.010 Chapter (A) of the
  ordinance, It is also the intent of this chapter to preserve and enhance property
  values through conserving and enhancing the distinctive and unique aesthetic
  character of many areas in the city. Sounds more on the line of economic
  development. Should add or change to historical preservation and the look of the
  City instead of property value. And also necessary for animal habitat.

  Under Section B(1) - No protected trees as herein defined shall be removed or
  damaged except in conformance with the provisions of this chapter Later in
  ordinance any tree can be removed as long as it is replaced. This is a direct
  contradiction.

  Commissioner Corona – Some people are annoyed by the trees and one neighbor
  wish they didn’t have the City tree on their property. There should be more
  information out there regarding the importance of trees.

  Commissioner Chan requested for City staff to assist.
  Staff volunteered to contact Community Development to get clarification on some of
  the sections of the ordinance. Commissioner Chan suggested to change section (B)

  Page 4 of 7
   ITEM #2
(1) to include all protected trees including trees located in the rear and side yard of
single-family dwellings. Also expand the species of protected trees as well.

Commissioner Corona – Ordinance should apply to all private and public property.
Rear and side yards should be included with the protection of trees. If there is an oak
tree in someone’s rear yard, they would need a permit to remove it. A Permit is
required to remove the tree. Commissioner Corona also noted if a protected tree
would like to be removed a permit is required except. Trees located in the back of the
house are not protected and should be included.

Commissioners requested clarity on why the trees in the rear of the house are not
protected.

Commissioner Chan stated that community members should understand the
protection is for California native trees only. Also, to strengthen the protection it
should be applied to both public and private property trees. Commissioner Corona
and Massaro agreed.

Commission Chan read and reviewed Section (B)(2) and agreed with the
requirements.

Commission Corona wanted to know what an entitlement application in regards to
section B(2)(a) combined permit; A separate tree permit is not required when a tree
removal is requested as part of an entitlement application. However, all other
provisions of this chapter apply and must be considered by the Planning Commission
as part of the combined development permit. Staff advised when someone needs an
approval to develop for a specific use.

Commissioner Chan wanted to know if the Environmental Sustainability Commission
(ESC) can be one of the entities that review the permit application for tree removal.
Staff advised the request should be submitted to the City Council as the code can only
be changed or amended by their approval. Elaborating on the “work that is so
extensive” from section B(1). Staff advised it is up to the Community Development
Director to determine if the work is extensive.

Commission Chan: In regards to section B(2)(a), how does the Planning Commission
determine the planning process? Also, the ESC would like to be part of the process.
The planning commission have legal authority to approve. Staff advised the ESC is
an advisory Commission only.

Commissioner Chan reviewed section B(2)(b)- Cases of emergency where the
Community Development Director or the Director of Public Works or their designees,
or any member of a law enforcement agency or Fire Department, in the performance
of his or her duties, determines that protected tree poses an imminent threat to the
public safety, or general welfare. Without questioning the Director of Public Works
capability of determining an emergency, Commissioner Chan asked was there an
arborist? Staff advised PW does have a part time Tree Maintenance person on staff.

  Page 5 of 7
   ITEM #2
  Staff explained imminent danger to the Commission as harmful to people and
  property in a short amount of time.

  The following sections of B(2) were discussed:

  (c) Visual barriers. Removal or relocation of protected trees necessary to obtain
  adequate line-of-sight distances for traffic safety as required by the Community
  Development Director or the Director of Public Works Services or their designees.
  Commission agreed that it makes sense only as a last resort
  (e) Routine trimming. Normal and routine trimming or pruning which does not result
  in damage or death to a tree. Removal of deadwood is allowed without a permit.
  Commissioner Massaro wanted to know what deadwood was and Commissioner
  Massaro mentioned it could be dead tree limbs and branch. Staff indicated it could be
  tree stumps as well.

  (f) Fruit trees. Any fruit tree may be trimmed or removed without a permit.
  Commission agreed to keep the restriction if a fully established fruit tree would not be
  able to be removed.

  (g) Palm trees. Any palm tree, except as listed as California native, may be trimmed
  or removed without a permit. Commissioner Chan agreed because some palm trees
  are invasive and bad for California and our region. Once the tree is removed it should
  be replaced with a California native tree or plant of similar size. Commissioners
  Massaro and Corona agreed.

  Commissioner Chan moved to continue review of the Tree Preservation Ordinance to
  the next Commission meeting.

•  PUBLIC COMMENT

  Received 1 speaker request cards from Sandy Lee.

  Ms. Lee wanted the Commission to also consider protection for post planting.
  Additionally, there are some things that you need to do to remove a tree and plant a
  tree to make it thrive. This includes some pre-care which can be added to section
  23.08.030 and anything else that will help the trees survive.

  Commissioner Chan stated it takes 3-5 years of consistent watering for a tree to
  survive on its own.

  According to Ms. Lee, Tree City USA donated 50 trees to the City. The Parks and
  Recreation Department planted the trees at Alhambra Park and none survived. Sandy
  Lee provided solutions and discussed the need to consult an arborist.

  Page 6 of 7
   ITEM #2
•  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION

  Commissioner Chan- Since the next meeting falls on November 9, 2023, and City
  Hall will be closed in observance of Veteran’s Day, Commissioners were asked if
  they would like to hold a special meeting; Commissioners agreed to November 16,
  2023.

  Staff will check the date to make sure it is available and will provide an alternate date
  if necessary.

•  ADJOURNMENT
  Commissioner Chan motioned to adjourn the meeting at 6:59 PM, Commissioner
  Massaro seconded. Motion unanimously approved.

  Page 7 of 7
   ITEM #3

Environmental Sustainability Commission Meeting- November 16, 2023
Update Items

  1. Bike & Pedestrian Plans

  On October 23, the consultant presented an overview to the Council and advised the next steps
  are to go out to the community to share the pedestrian improvement priority zones as well as
  bike network. There are different phases associated with the bike network, since the
  installation of some classifications may require further study. Opportunity to attend an
  information meeting is available throughout the month of November and posted on the City’s
  website.

  2. Sustainability Plan

  Consultant will provide an update on the Sustainability Plan at the meeting.

  3. Turf Replacement Rebate

  The San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District (SGVMWD) has submitted the application for
  the DWR Drought Relief Grant to provide assistance to its member agencies to fund a turf
  replacement rebate program. The project was not funded this year, but it did rank near the top
  of the line. Where it fell short was in two places:

  •  Letters of Support from all member agencies
  •  Added technical details on projects.

  SGVMWD is considering re-applying once the grant opens up again.

  4. Organic Waste Recycling Program

  •  Organics Recycling Business Workshop – Republic Services and the City of Alhambra
  hosted a workshop for businesses to learn about new organics recycling requirements
  set by State Senate Bill 1383 on November 16, 2023. Office hours were conducted from
  10AM to 12:30PM, and a short presentation was made at 11AM. Topics included the
  social, economic, and environmental benefits of organics recycling; diversion, container,
  education, and food recovery requirements of businesses; best practices and resources;
  and handout of free indoor organics containers and compostable bags to get started.
  Businesses not able to participate are encouraged to visit bit.ly/AlhambraOrganics to
  obtain all the resources presented or e-mail recycle@cityofalhambra.org.

  •  SB 1383 Local Assistance Grant – The City of Alhambra submitted an application for
  CalRecycle’s SB 1383 Local Assistance Grant to fund implementation of organics
  recycling mandates issued by the state. The grant application included new equipment
  for City staff to apply recovered organic waste products at City parks and medians, a
  professional advertising firm to circulate material made from the Alhambra Recycles
   ITEM #3

  Campaign, and new outdoor and indoor recycling & organic waste receptacles for high-
  trafficked City facilities and Alhambra businesses.

  •  Organics Recycling at City Facilities – City staff have rolled out organics collection
  services and containers at City facilities including City Hall, Police Department, Library
  Civic Center, CSC Center, Fire Department 71-74, and City Yard. Literature and education
  were shared to all staff members, and outreach is ongoing by the City’s Recycling
  Assistant.

  •  Alhambra Recycles Champaign – City Staff will provide a presentation to the
  Commission.

5. Safe Clean Water Program (SCWP)
  The City has submitted an application for funding the Green Street Demonstration Project on
  Main St.
  • Application for construction costs was submitted to the Safe Clean Water Program
  (SCWP) FY 2024-25 call for projects by the deadline, July 31, 2023. The project is
  currently being review by the SCWP Scoring Committee
  • Contract was awarded for design on 9/26/23.
